title: Minnesota officials say US government stopped sharing evidence on fatal ICE shootings
summary:
The federal government has stopped sharing evidence with Minnesota authorities who are investigating the killings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti by federal officers during a violent anti-immigration, anti-protest crackdown in the state earlier this year, state officials said in recent court filings.
Minnesota officials sued the Trump administration in March for access to materials they said they needed to independently investigate the shootings.
Advertisement AdvertisementThe Trump administration has suggested that state prosecutors don't have jurisdiction to investigate federal officers, while Minnesota officials have said they don't trust the federal government to investigate itself.
State prosecutors announced in July that the federal government had begun turning over evidence in the cases, including police body-camera video and hard drives containing statements.
But Minnesota investigators said in October court filings that the transfer of evidence stopped soon after the July announcement.

title: These 26 current US House representatives were born outside the US
summary:
Similar to the US Senate, members of the House of Representatives do not need to be natural-born citizens in order to take office.
The House of Representatives, one of the two chambers of Congress alongside the Senate, has 435 voting members.
To qualify as a US House representative, a person must be:At least 25 years oldA US citizen for at least seven years.
Many current House members were US citizens at birth despite being born in another country — for instance, because they were born to American parents working in government positions abroad.
Here are the 26 active House representatives born outside the US.

title: Canada grants asylum to 7,643 Nigerians in 30 months
summary:
Canada granted refugee protection to no fewer than 7,643 Nigerians over 30 months spanning January 2024 to June 2026, fresh data from the Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada showed.
However, Canadian authorities rejected the asylum claims of 3,080 Nigerians during the same period, meaning nearly three in every 10 Nigerians whose cases were decided were denied asylum.
A further 1,530 Nigerian cases were either abandoned or withdrawn, bringing the total number of Nigerian cases finalised in Canada during the period to 12,253.
As of December 31, 2024, the board recorded 19,889 Nigerian cases awaiting a decision—a backlog nearly six times the total cases finalised that year.
Across the 30-month window, Canada finalised 202,878 refugee claims from all nationalities, accepting 118,656 and rejecting 34,546.

title: OPINION: Germany is having the wrong immigration debate
summary:
Both in politics and online, the debate around immigration tends to focus on limiting 'irregular immigration'.
Social researcher Andreas Herteux argues Germany should be more concerned with the skilled workers who are leaving.
The 260,000 people who left are therefore neither 260,000 skilled workers nor 260,000 refugees, but a mix of both and others.
Skilled workers and integrated immigrants tend to be better equipped to leave Germany and move elsewhere.
People who experienced discrimination more frequently were significantly more likely to express thoughts of leaving Germany and concrete plans to do so.

title: Justice Department orders California counties to set aside ballots from suspected noncitizens
summary:
The Justice Department on Friday ordered California election officials to identify suspected noncitizens on voter rolls and set aside their mail-in ballots — warning that officials who knowingly count ballots cast by noncitizens could face criminal liability.
So far, officials have found most of the records belong to voters who are no longer actively registered in the county, County Clerk Tricia Webber told CNN on Saturday.
But some states, including California, have passed laws allowing noncitizens to cast ballots in local or school board elections.
